title: WF03 f5 batch3 step04: PostgreSQL result rows leaked column buffers across OBS-03/OBS-04 and masked TC-IDN-02-05
summary: Resolved the batch3 Step04 backend integration blocker by fixing PostgreSQL result cleanup so query/queryRow callers release per-column buffers, eliminating the DebugAllocator leak traces seen in OBS-03 audit pagination, OBS-04 timeline reads, and the aggregate path that had masked ADM-UI-09 confirmation behind TC-IDN-02-05.

root_cause.details: The PostgreSQL client deinitialized only row slices, not the duplicated column buffers allocated in parseDataRow. Query-heavy integration paths therefore leaked on every successful read. A follow-on regression in src/db/pool.zig queryRow also lacked guaranteed result cleanup on every exit path.

changes: Updated vendor/pg/pg.zig Result.deinit to free every non-null column buffer before freeing each row slice.
Updated src/db/pool.zig queryRow to defer result cleanup across all exits and to free copied zero-length slices correctly on error.
Revalidated the dedicated OBS-03 and OBS-04 integration targets plus the aggregate blocker rerun for TC-IDN-02-05.

follow_up_verification.summary: Rework verification found the allocator-cleanup fix already present in the working tree. After clearing a locked zig-out executable from a running bpm-platform process, the required aggregate validation commands both exited 0 and no OBS-04 DebugAllocator leak reproduced.

commands.evidence: Build completed successfully after stopping the running bpm-platform.exe that held zig-out/bin/bpm-platform.exe open on Windows.
Completed without build errors after stopping the locked bpm-platform process.

prevention: Whenever a DB client stores per-cell duplicated buffers, deinit must walk both the row list and each column allocation instead of freeing only container slices.
In wrapper helpers like queryRow, use defer-based cleanup so early returns and copy failures cannot bypass result deallocation.
